title: GUARDIAN: Safeguarding LLM Multi-Agent Collaborations with Temporal Graph Modeling
evidence: adaptive=0: attacks are simulated, not defense-aware ('we simulate errors through agent-targeted attacks (randomly selecting 1 agent...)'); no adaptive/optimized attack, no limitation text on it. Unsupervised temporal-graph autoencoder (BERT node embeddings) scores agent nodes each round and removes highest-anomaly agent+edges before next round. Covers hallucination amplification (non-adversarial) and agent/communication-targeted error injection. Backbones GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Llama-3.1-8B. Reports anomaly detection rate, not FPR.

title: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
evidence: Non-adversarial: no threat/attacker/adversary terms in paper; goal = data minimization of UI uploaded to cloud LLM. Local LLM ranks layout-aware UI blocks and only top block(s) are sent; cloud LLM may request more blocks. Privacy metric = UI exposure reduction (55.6%) and sensitive-element reduction (70.49% DroidTask). Models: cloud GPT-4o + local Gemma2-9B/Qwen2.5-7B/LLaMA3.1-8B. Overhead: latency 1.49-1.66x, cloud tokens ~0.94-1.15x. arxiv_v1 from paperswithcode mirror date (abs history page not retrievable). judge_exposed=Y only in the literal sense (local LLM reads full screen content).

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.12104v2 (arXiv v2, 2025-10-24; v3 2026-03-26 exists, comment 'Accepted to NeurIPS 2025')
evidence: adaptive=2: 'two types of adaptive attacks: the curated adaptive attack and the PAIR attack'; 'we sample several cases where DRIFT successfully defends but the base agent does not, and optimize an injection prompt that can bypass the isolator and validator' (GPT-4o-mini, AgentDojo; ASR +0.31%). Secure Planner builds control/data-level policy from user query before tool interaction; Dynamic Validator (LLM, sees updated tool messages) approves deviations by privilege (Read/Write/Execute); Injection Isolator masks conflicting instructions in returned tool messages. User approval request is 'equivalent to rejecting' in eval, so burden not measured. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Claude-3-Haiku, Qwen2.5-7B (fine-tuned). Tokens ~1.89x.

title: PsySafe: A Comprehensive Framework for Psychological-based Attack, Defense, and Evaluation of Multi-agent System Safety
bench: own:PsySafe dataset (dangerous tasks from DAN/AdvBench + Camel safe tasks, tiny set 125);AutoGen
evidence: adaptive=0: no evaluation of attacks designed against the defenses; attacks are the paper's own dark-trait injections. Defenses: input filter (GPT-4, Llama Guard) on user input; Doctor defense (psych test + doctor agent rewrites contaminated agent's system prompt before actions); Police agent 'check[s] the safety of the responses from Agent1 and Agent2, and correct[s] them'. Defense eval only with GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 on AutoGen (Table 5); metrics danger rates/psych scores; no utility/overhead/FPR.

title: TrustAgent: Towards Safe and Trustworthy LLM-based Agents
bench: own:TrustAgent dataset (70 cases, 5 domains; everyday/finance cases adapted from ToolEmu);ToolEmu emulator
evidence: Non-adversarial: unintentional unsafe actions (no attacker). Pre-planning (regulation/hindsight fine-tuning, GPT-3.5 only) + in-planning (retrieved regulations in prompt) + post-planning GPT-4 safety inspector that 'assesses whether the action and the current trajectory violates any retrieved regulations', asks agent to revise, halts on repeated violation. Constitution = human/GPT-4-drafted regulations, manually checked (applied by LLM, no deterministic rule). public_bench=Y only via ToolEmu-derived cases. Models: GPT-4-1106, GPT-3.5-turbo-1106, Claude-2, Claude-instant-1.2, Mixtral-8x7B. Metrics: safety, helpfulness, correct steps; no cost. arxiv_v1 not retrievable (ID implies 2024-02).

title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
evidence: adaptive=0: no attack designed against the GNN; limitations do not discuss it. Supervised GNN (MiniLM utterance embeddings, trained on labeled attack data) flags high-risk agents per round and prunes their outgoing edges; 'G-Safeguard cannot preemptively prevent the MAS from being compromised'. Threats: prompt injection, memory poisoning, tool attack. Models GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, LLaMA-3.1-70B, Claude-3.5-Haiku, DeepSeek-V3. Reports ASR, system accuracy, attacker recognition accuracy; no cost or FPR.

title: AGrail: A Lifelong Agent Guardrail with Effective and Adaptive Safety Detection
evidence: adaptive=0: evaluated only on existing/own attack sets (prompt injection, system sabotage, environment attack, EIA, AdvWeb); no defense-aware attack incl. on its memory. 'If S = False, the guardrail blocks the agent's action'. Analyzer+Executor LLMs generate/refine safety checks from safety criteria with lifelong memory (TTA), optionally call detection tools; inputs include agent actions and environment observations. 'Adaptive' in title = test-time adaptation. Guardrail LLMs: Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini (agents GPT-4-Turbo/GPT-4o). Benign: 'preserves 96% of benign actions'.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence: adaptive=0: fixed attacks only (Important Instructions, InjecAgent, Ignore Previous); limitation: 'If the defender LLM is weak or adversarially probed, extraction or scoring may fail'. Shield (same model as agent, separately prompted) extracts instructions and checks ContributesTo user task; flags misaligned tool outputs with feedback; 'prevents execution of misaligned calls'. Models GPT-4o (main), GPT-4o-mini, GPT-3.5-turbo. Latency median 62.56s vs 6.17s no defense; FPR not reported.

title: IPIGuard: A Novel Tool Dependency Graph-Based Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
evidence: adaptive=0: only mention is related work ('Recent studies on adaptive IPI attacks (Zhan et al., 2025) demonstrate ... bypass many model-level defenses'); attacks Ignore Previous, InjecAgent, Tool Knowledge, Important Instructions. Tool Dependency Graph planned from user instruction + tool descriptions + system context before any tool output; execution restricted to TDG; node expansion limited to query tools; fake tool invocation for injected calls. Executor LLM sees tool outputs only for argument estimation. Models GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen3-32B, o4-mini. arxiv_v1 not retrievable (arXiv 429; ID implies 2025-08).

title: SafeScientist: Enhancing AI Scientist Safety for Risk-Aware Scientific Discovery
evidence: adaptive=0: generic jailbreak/injection methods (DAN, DeepInception, Base64, Payload Splitting, LST, etc.) not adapted to the monitors. Prompt monitor = LLaMA-Guard-3-8B + SafeChecker LLM (fused reject); agent collaboration monitor (ethics agent) intervenes in multi-agent discussion; tool-use monitor with manually authored tool safety constraints blocks unsafe calls; paper ethic reviewer refines output. Utility = research quality scores. n_models: GPT-4o default + Table 6 variants (GPT-4.1, GPT-3.5-turbo, Qwen2.5-72B, Llama-3-70B) - defense-on status not fully confirmed. arxiv_v1 not retrievable (arXiv 429; ID implies 2025-05).

title: Privacy in Action: Towards Realistic Privacy Mitigation and Evaluation for LLM-Powered Agents
evidence: Non-adversarial: 'risk of inadvertent data leaks'; limitations say adversarial scenarios (e.g., memory poisoning) 'could disrupt flow extraction' but not evaluated. PrivacyChecker (contextual-integrity flow extraction + per-flow judgment; 'No' flows excluded/abstracted) deployed via system prompt, tool description, or standalone MCP tool send_privacy_check that 'receives both the drafted message and the action trajectory'. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, o1, Qwen3-8B/14B (thinking/non-thinking), DeepSeek-R1 (PrivacyLens); o3 (PrivacyLens-Live). Metrics: leak rate, helpfulness.

title: ALRPHFS: Adversarially Learned Risk Patterns with Hierarchical Fast & Slow Reasoning for Robust Agent Defense
evidence: adaptive=0: offline red-blue adversarial loop is used to build the risk-pattern DB (training), no test-time attack against the deployed defense. Fast path = hybrid embedding+BM25 retrieval vs risk patterns (block high-confidence); slow path = LLM reasoning with historical context incl. environment. Evaluated offline on logged trajectories ('offline simulation'), so no task utility; FPR reported. Models GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Haiku (GPT-4o only as red team). ~5000 tokens/task. arxiv_v1 not retrievable (ID implies 2025-05).

title: Don’t Click That: Teaching Web Agents to Resist Deceptive Interfaces
evidence: adaptive=0: manually curated + synthesized dark patterns, no deceptive designs crafted against DUDE; 'our evaluation relies on static screenshots ... we have not validated in fully interactive environments'. Separate GRPO-trained VLM evaluator judges each candidate click (deceptive/ineffective/legit); 'Only clicks judged benign proceed to execution'. Agents Qwen3-VL-4B, UI-TARS-1.5-7B, GLM-4.6V-Flash (evaluators Qwen3-VL-2B / UI-TARS-1.5-7B). Metrics SR, DFR; benign-click rejection rate not reported. arxiv_v1 from paperswithcode mirror date.

title: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
evidence: adaptive=0: no attack designed against OS-Sentinel. Formal verifier (file-system hash integrity, curated sensitive lexicon, regex) + VLM contextual judge on screenshot-action pairs; outputs safe/unsafe flags (strict OR / consensus AND). Evaluated offline on frozen trajectories (trajectory acc/F1, step-level delay-penalized score); no live blocking experiment, so A_mode=post and decisions are flag-only. Covers malicious use/prompt injection and agent-side unintended risks. Judges GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, gpt-oss-120B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B. arxiv_v1 not retrievable (ID implies 2025-10).

title: VIGIL: Defending LLM Agents Against Tool-Stream Injection via Verify-Before-Commit
evidence: adaptive=0: no defense-aware or optimized attack; 'adaptive' only refers to VIGIL's backtracking. Attack vectors: explicit directive, dependency trap, feature inducement, runtime hijacking, error hijacking, content injection. Intent Anchor LLM derives constraints from user query only; Perception Sanitizer LLM strips directives from (untrusted) tool descriptions/feedback; Speculative Reasoner + Grounding Verifier check candidate trajectories (action metadata vs constraints, entailment) before commit; failure triggers backtracking. Constraint check performed by LLM verifier (no deterministic rule confirmed). Models Qwen3-max, Gemini-2.5-pro, GPT-4o (appendix).
